web_evidence.title: Stephen King on Christine
web_evidence.note: In a direct interview, King confirms that Dennis tells the opening and closing in first person while the middle was written in third person after Dennis's hospitalization; he describes the middle as reportage-like and notionally attributable to Dennis.

web_evidence.title: Rereading Stephen King: week 15 – Christine
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly reports that most of the novel uses Dennis's first-person narration but a sustained hospital-period section switches to third-person omniscient.

web_evidence.title: The Great Stephen King Reread: Christine
web_evidence.note: The structural review specifies first-person Dennis narration in the opening and closing portions and a substantial third-person middle portion.

person_note: The quote sample repeatedly exposes Dennis as a participating first-person narrator and also contains a third-person Part Two scene. The authorized opening corroborates Dennis's first-person voice, while King's own explanation and multiple independent structural accounts establish a sustained third-person middle followed by a return to Dennis's first person. King conceptually calls the middle 'masked' first-person reportage, creating a narrator-theory ambiguity about Dennis as implied compiler, but the methodology classifies sustained sections written in different narrative persons as ALTERNATING. No credible source indicates second-person narration or a different overall structure.
